name: Call Ratio Spread 1x2 (Call Front Spread)
summary: Buy one nearer call and sell two further-OTM calls in the same expiry, usually for a credit; profits most if the underlying drifts up to the short strike, with unlimited risk above it.

legs.strike_rule: Long call at-the-money or slightly ITM, 0.45-0.60 delta.
Two short calls at 0.20-0.30 delta, far enough out that the structure opens for a net credit.

max_profit: (short strike - long strike) * 100 + net credit, achieved exactly at the short strike at expiry
max_loss: UNDEFINED above the short strike -- one of the two short calls is uncovered and loses without limit
breakevens: lower: long strike - credit per share (if opened for credit there is no lower breakeven -- the credit is kept); upper: short strike + (max profit per share)

greeks.delta: slightly positive at entry (+0.05 to +0.15 per unit), turning sharply negative as price approaches the short strike
greeks.gamma: negative, and increasingly so near the short strike
greeks.theta: positive while price is below the short strike
greeks.vega: negative -- you are net short one option

when_to_use: When you expect a slow drift higher that stalls at a known resistance level, and IV rank is elevated so the two short calls pay well. A favorite of experienced premium sellers; structurally a trap for automated systems because the profit peak sits exactly where the risk begins.
entry_rules: BLOCKED ON THIS ACCOUNT. Of the two short calls, only one is covered by the long call; the second is naked. That is Level 4 authority, which Alpaca does not offer, and Alpaca's MLeg engine explicitly rejects orders containing an uncovered short call leg.
Defined-risk substitute: a call broken-wing butterfly (buy 1 lower call, sell 2 middle calls, buy 1 further-out call) -- same shape, capped upside risk, and Level 3 legal as a four-leg MLeg.

If it were enabled: IV rank >= 40; net credit > $0.00; short strike at or above a resistance level tested at least twice in the last 60 sessions; DTE 30-45; upper breakeven at least 1.5 ATR(20) above spot.
Alpaca ratio note: leg_ratio values must reduce to GCD 1, so 1:2 is a valid ratio shape -- the rejection here is about coverage, not about the ratio itself.
management_rules: If enabled: take profit at 50% of max profit, or close for any credit once the underlying is within 1% of the short strike.
Stop: close the entire structure if the underlying trades above the upper breakeven, or if position delta reaches -0.50 per unit.
Never let it run into expiry hoping to pin the short strike.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: if the short calls are ITM at 15:30 ET on expiry day, closing is mandatory -- assignment on two contracts against one long call leaves 100 short shares per unit.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close whenever the short calls are ITM with extrinsic < $0.10.
DIVIDEND GUARD: close before ex-dividend whenever the short calls are ITM and extrinsic < 1.5 * dividend.
assignment_risk: High. Two short calls, only one covered. Assignment on both delivers 200 short shares per unit against 100 shares of long-call coverage, leaving 100 naked short shares.
buying_power: The covered pair holds the vertical's width; the extra short call holds Reg-T naked call margin. Not available on Alpaca.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 on both strikes; the 2-lot short leg needs quoted size >= 20.
common_mistakes: Being drawn in by 'free' upside to the short strike; not realizing the peak profit point is also the danger point; running it into earnings; assuming a credit entry means no risk.
zero_dte_notes: Not permitted, and 0DTE ratio spreads have the sharpest possible transition from max profit to unbounded loss.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
